n_flag: n=3 female test speakers -- within-sample, not a population claim
sex_subspace_dim_rationale: Binary female-vs-male contrast has exactly one degree of freedom between the two group means -- the whitened logistic-regression direction is rank-1 by construction, consistent with every other sex-direction estimator in this repo. k=1 reported explicitly per row (sex_subspace_dim column), not silently assumed.
sex_subspace_fit_population: SI test fold (12 speakers, 9M/3F) -- per pre-registration, NOT the train+val fold used by geom_within_digit.py's (b)/(c) measures (that choice trades power for evaluation-population consistency with the digit-gradient, computed on the same fold).
digit_gradient_population: SI test fold, same 12 speakers / 6000 utterances as the sex-subspace fit.
digit_gradient_aggregation: unit-normalize each utterance's gradient, top eigenvector of the mean outer-product matrix (sign-invariant, avoids signed cancellation across utterances with different correct digits).
pre_registered_expectation: CONFIRMATORY: the digit-gradient stays >=~80 degrees from the sex subspace at every layer in both architectures, consistent with the penultimate result -- no layer where the decision aligns with sex. Written before running; watching for any layer that drops well below that as the interesting exception.
claim_boundary: GEOMETRIC claim only: near-orthogonality means the decision axis does not align with sex at that layer. Bounds alignment/pathway, not strict necessity (would need perturbation, out of scope here). Confidence comes from cross-layer/cross-architecture/cross-seed consistency, not from the female sample size (n=3).
decision_rule: All layers near-orthogonal (angle >= null, both archs, seed-stable) -> whole-pipeline geometric support for 'not used'. A seed-stable layer below the null -> interesting exception, flagged, not overclaimed as necessity. Seed-unstable -> inconclusive at that layer.
overall_verdict_text: Every layer, every seed, both architectures: the digit-gradient direction stays at/above the random-subspace null relative to the sex subspace (never seed-stably below it). The digit decision's gradient does not align with sex anywhere in the pipeline -- whole-pipeline geometric support for 'not used', broadening the penultimate-only readout result. This is a geometric/alignment claim, not a necessity claim (no perturbation was run here).
